2014|newspaper=Bangor Daily News|date=September 5, 2014}} * [[David Slagger]], former [[Maliseet people|Maliseet]] representative to the [[Maine House of Representatives]] (originally declared as a Democrat, switched parties, then unenrolled) ====Declined==== * [[Shawn Moody]], businessman and candidate for governor [[2010 Maine gubernatorial election|in 2010]]{{cite news|url=http://www.pressherald.com/blogs/capitolticker/214379251.html|title=Shawn Moody making another run for gov? Maybe.|last=Mistler|first=Steve|date=July 9, 2013|work=[[Portland Press Herald]]|access-date=July 9, 2013|archive-date=September 17, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130917011905/http://www.pressherald.com/blogs/capitolticker/214379251.html|url-status=dead}} ==General election== ===Candidates=== * Eliot Cutler (Independent), attorney, board member of [[Americans Elect]] and candidate for governor [[2010 Maine gubernatorial election|in 2010]] * [[Paul LePage]] (Republican), incumbent governor * [[Mike Michaud]] (Democratic), U.S. representative ===Campaign=== On January 17, 2014, Eliot Cutler announced that he had challenged LePage and Michaud to a series of policy debates, with at least one to be held in each of Maine's [[Counties of Maine|16 counties]], over the course of the campaign. Cutler noted that neither man had a primary challenger and as such the field is largely set, with plenty of time to debate. Both LePage and Michaud's campaigns criticized Cutler as issuing such a challenge only to jump-start his campaign and generate attention.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/01/17/politics/lepage-and-michaud-call-cutlers-debate-challenge-a-stunt/|title=LePage and Michaud call Cutler's debate challenge a stunt|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=January 17, 2014 |access-date=January 17, 2014}} Lee Schultheis said that his campaign was not about winning the election, but about encouraging honest conversation on the issues and working towards compromise, while criticizing the win-at-any-cost mentality in politics. He summarized his campaign as "I'm running for Governor, but not really". He had qualified for the ballot and as such had been invited to at least one debate.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/06/23/politics/maine-has-a-fourth-gubernatorial-candidate-running-for-the-2014-election-but-not-really/|title=LePage and Michaud call Cutler's debate challenge a stunt|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=July 23, 2014 |access-date=August 1, 2014}} However, citing the fact that two of three debates he had been invited to had been cancelled, as well as the difficulty of an independent working in the two-party system, he withdrew from the race on September 5, 2014. Cutler posted a video to his [[Facebook]] and [[Twitter]] accounts on May 5, 2014, where he responded to a voter's question about his candidacy potentially [[Vote splitting|splitting the vote]] again. He stated that his supporters, if they felt on the night before the election that he could not win, should vote for someone else.{{cite news|url=http://pollways.bangordailynews.com/2014/05/06/maine-politics/cutler-gives-supporters-permission-to-vote-for-someone-else/|title=Cutler gives supporters permission to vote for someone else|newspaper=Bangor Daily News|date=May 6, 2014|access-date=May 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140509070411/http://pollways.bangordailynews.com/2014/05/06/maine-politics/cutler-gives-supporters-permission-to-vote-for-someone-else/|archive-date=May 9, 2014|url-status=dead}} In July 2014, Cutler claimed that in May 2011 he had been approached by [[Maine Democratic Party]] Chairman Ben Grant to run as a Democrat in 2014, with assurances that the Party would "clear the field" in such a circumstance. Grant denied Cutler's claim, calling it "100 percent false", stating that while he had met with Cutler, that subject was not discussed. He added that the party had been focused solely on getting Mike Michaud or [[Chellie Pingree]] to run for governor. Cutler stated that he would be willing to sign an affidavit on the matter, as he remembered the conversation "very clearly". Attorney and Democratic activist [[Severin Beliveau]] disputed Cutler's claim that he had been offered a "cleared field", saying: "That's [Cutler's] ego. We all have egos, but his is in another world, in the ether somewhere." Cutler further claimed that in the spring of 2011 he was asked by then-[[Maine Republican Party]] Chairman Charlie Webster to join the Republican Party. Webster also repudiated Cutler's claim, saying that he only met Cutler as a courtesy, asking "why would Republicans want a candidate who doesn't share our views? That doesn't make sense."{{cite web|url=http://www.centralmaine.com/2014/07/26/cutler-says-democrats-asked-him-to-run-in-2014/|title=Cutler says Democrats asked him to run in 2014|publisher=Kennebec Journal |date=July 26, 2014 |access-date=July 27, 2014}} LePage stated on a WVOM-FM radio show on August 7 that he believes he will either win by a landslide or lose by a landslide, stating that his views are too different from his opponents' to result in a close race.{{cite web|url=http://www.wcsh6.com/story/news/local/augusta-waterville/2014/08/07/lepage-ill-either-win-or-lose-by-a-landslide/13742283/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140811234431/http://www.wcsh6.com/story/news/local/augusta-waterville/2014/08/07/lepage-ill-either-win-or-lose-by-a-landslide/13742283/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 11, 2014|title=LePage: I'll either win or lose by a 'landslide'|publisher=WCSH-6 TV|date=August 7, 2014|access-date=August 7, 2014}} On September 18, LePage told the editorial board of ''[[The Portsmouth Herald]]'' that he did not want their endorsement, saying his interest in it was "none, zero". He further stated "I'm not about politics. I'm about issues. I do not want be endorsed. I don't want to be mentioned in the same vein as Mike Michaud."{{cite web|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/20/politics/lepage-bets-gop-will-take-maine-house-in-2014/|title=LePage bets GOP will take Maine House in 2014|publisher=Bangor Daily News/York Weekly |date=September 20, 2014 |access-date=September 20, 2014}} In mid-October, it was reported that the Maine Republican Party had begun spending money to target Democratic voters with negative attacks against Michaud that also praised Cutler, in believing Cutler would play a spoiler role.{{cite web|url=http://thetippingpoint.bangordailynews.com/2014/10/18/state-politics/republican-party-begins-spending-to-boost-cutler/|title=Republican Party begins spending to boost Cutler|publisher=Bangor Daily News/York Weekly|author=Mike Tipping|date=October 18, 2014|access-date=October 18, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019231004/http://thetippingpoint.bangordailynews.com/2014/10/18/state-politics/republican-party-begins-spending-to-boost-cutler/|archive-date=October 19, 2014|url-status=dead}} LePage had previously said in June that Cutler's candidacy was good for his re-election campaign.{{cite web|url=http://www.wmtw.com/politics/candidates-for-governor-campaign-in-southern-maine/26306698#!UqZTC|title=Candidates for governor campaign in southern Maine|publisher=WMTW |author=Paul Merrill |date=June 3, 2014 |access-date=October 18, 2014}} Meanwhile, Cutler himself has appeared to be winding down his campaign, decreasing his spending on television advertisements, leading to speculation that he was essentially conceding the race.{{cite news|url=http://contributors.pressherald.com/politics/agree-to-disagree/cutler-pulling-stakes/|title=Is Cutler pulling up stakes?|newspaper=Portland Press Herald|author=Ethan Strimling|date=October 2, 2014|access-date=October 18, 2014|archive-date=October 21, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021164502/http://contributors.pressherald.com/politics/agree-to-disagree/cutler-pulling-stakes/|url-status=dead}} By the end of October, this seemed to be confirmed, as columnist [[Ethan Strimling]] noted that Cutler's weekly TV spending had decreased across October from $55,000 to $50,000, then $29,000, down to $4,000. By contrast, campaign committees and outside groups supporting LePage and Michaud were outspending him 100-to-1 each.{{cite news|url=http://contributors.pressherald.com/politics/agree-to-disagree/cutler-pulling-stakes-part-ii/|title=Cutler campaign goes dark|newspaper=Portland Press Herald|author=Ethan Strimling|date=October 20, 2014|access-date=October 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141024054350/http://contributors.pressherald.com/politics/agree-to-disagree/cutler-pulling-stakes-part-ii/|archive-date=October 24, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} In late October, the [[Republican Governors Association]] began airing a television advertisement that attacked Michaud before pivoting to praise Cutler, noting that he had been endorsed by Independent U.S. Senator and former Independent Governor [[Angus King]]. The spot did not mention LePage, hoping instead to persuade Michaud supporters to vote for Cutler. Michaud campaign manager Matt McTighe called it "a desperate attempt to split the vote that is uniting to defeat Gov. LePage"{{cite web|url=http://www.msnbc.com/rachel-maddow-show/republican-governors-association-exploits-its-pawn-maine|title=Republican Governors Association exploits its pawn in Maine|publisher=MSNBC|author=Steve Benen |author-link=Steve Benen|date=October 28, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} and King, despite having endorsed Cutler, accused the RGA of "trying to trick people" and called their tactics "[dis]honest... they're trying to promote one candidate when they're really trying to promote someone else."{{cite news|url=http://contributors.pressherald.com/politics/capitol-ticker/angus-king-rga-ad-boosting-cutler-tries-trick-people/|title=Angus King: RGA ad boosting Cutler tries to 'trick people'|newspaper=Portland Press Herald|author=Steve Mistler|date=October 28, 2014|access-date=October 29, 2014|archive-date=October 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029160802/http://contributors.pressherald.com/politics/capitol-ticker/angus-king-rga-ad-boosting-cutler-tries-trick-people/|url-status=dead}} After Cutler announced that he would hold a press conference on October 29, it was speculated that he was doing so to withdraw from the race.{{cite web|url=http://politicalwire.com/archives/2014/10/29/will_cutler_drop_out_in_maine.html|title=Will Cutler Drop Out In Maine?|publisher=Political Wire|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=October 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141030004830/http://politicalwire.com/archives/2014/10/29/will_cutler_drop_out_in_maine.html|archive-date=October 30, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} Cutler did not announce his withdrawal but did say that he was a "realist" and acknowledged that any victory by him would be a "long shot". He said that his supporters should "vote their consciences", whether that be for LePage or Michaud. Cutler went on to say that he would not withdraw to "kowtow to party politics and allow a bunch of political polls to drown out the voices of thousands of Mainers who believe that standing for principles, ideals and ideas makes you an American, not a spoiler." However, his announcement was seen by many as "an acknowledgement that [his] campaign is over."{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/10/29/politics/cutler-to-make-election-announcement-at-impromptu-news-conference-wednesday-morning/|title=Cutler says victory is 'long shot,' tells supporters to vote accordingly|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}}{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/politics/articles/2014-10-29/cutler-trailing-in-maine-says-hes-hopeful-but-a-realist|title=Cutler, Trailing In Maine, Says He's 'Hopeful' But a 'Realist'|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|publisher=Bloomberg|date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}}{{cite news|url=http://www.pressherald.com/2014/10/29/cutler-to-hold-press-conference-wednesday-morning/|title=Cutler staying in race, insists Mainers should 'vote their conscience'|newspaper=Portland Press Herald |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} Cutler also encouraged Maine voters to support a proposed citizen initiative to implement [[Instant-runoff voting|ranked choice voting]]. Immediately after his press conference, a group of former Cutler supporters reiterated their backing of Michaud, saying that "the right thing now is to unite behind Mike Michaud."{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2014/oct/29/you-dont-have-to-vote-for-me-maine-gubernatorial-candidate-tells-supporters|title=You don't have to vote for me, Maine gubernatorial candidate tells supporters|newspaper=The Guardian |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} Shortly after, Angus King announced that he was switching his endorsement from Cutler to Michaud, explaining: "it is clear that the voters of Maine are not prepared to elect Eliot... The good news is that we still have a chance to elect a governor who will represent the majority of Maine people: my friend and colleague, Mike Michaud."{{cite news|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/eliot-cutler_n_6067914|title=Eliot Cutler Staying In Maine Governors Race But Tells Backers To 'Vote Their Conscience'|work=The Huffington Post|date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}}{{cite news|url=http://www.pressherald.com/2014/10/29/angus-king-switches-endorsement-from-cutler-to-michaud/|title=Angus King switches endorsement from Cutler to Michaud|newspaper=Portland Press Herald |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} Cutler stated that he was "obviously disappointed" by King's change.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/10/29/politics/elections/snowe-endorses-lepage-as-king-switches-gubernatorial-nod-from-cutler-to-michaud/|title=King switches gubernatorial nod from Cutler to Michaud; Snowe robocall to boost LePage|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} ====Debates==== The Michaud campaign stated on July 30 that Michaud would only participate in debates where LePage is present and not attend ones where Cutler is the only other participant, because: "we are running against Paul LePage, he's who we are looking to unseat". The LePage campaign has said they will schedule debates around the Governor's work schedule and priorities and declined to participate in a debate in the [[Lewiston, Maine|Lewiston]]/[[Auburn, Maine|Auburn]] area in September. Cutler criticized both men as "cowards" and said that they wanted voters to make their decision "on the basis of a cascade of negative television ads bought by outside special interests". Michaud's campaign responded that at least four debates have been scheduled so far.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/07/31/news/lewiston-auburn/lepage-michaud-arent-interested-in-many-public-debates/|title=LePage, Michaud aren't interested in many public debates|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=July 30, 2014 |access-date=July 31, 2014}} Despite Michaud's position on debates, he did appear at a forum on September 12 to discuss energy policy topics with only Cutler, after LePage abruptly withdrew from participating, citing what he called a change in the format of the event. The LePage campaign stated that they had thought each candidate would appear on stage separately, but learned the day of the event that the candidates would share a stage. LePage said: "If you set up a format, you've got to stick to that format" and his campaign said event organizers "attempted to arrange a setting to put politics ahead of public policy". They denied the withdrawal was politically motivated to force Michaud to debate Cutler.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/12/politics/elections/lepage-skips-candidates-heating-fuel-forum-in-portland/|title=LePage objects to format of Portland energy forum, drops out|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=September 12, 2014 |access-date=September 15, 2014}} Both the Michaud and Cutler campaigns stated they were aware of the format. Cutler offered to leave the stage while LePage spoke, but that did not change LePage's mind. Event organizers stated "there was no intent to place politics before policy" and that the issue distracted from their efforts to discuss energy policy.{{cite web|url=http://www.centralmaine.com/2014/09/12/gov-paul-lepage-refuses-to-appear-at-energy-forum/|title=Gov. Paul LePage refuses to appear at energy forum|publisher=Kennebec Journal |date=September 12, 2014 |access-date=September 15, 2014}} LePage told [[WMTW (TV)|WMTW]] Channel 8 on September 22 that he was considering not participating in any debates with Michaud,{{cite web|url=http://www.wmtw.com/politics/gov-lepage-says-he-may-not-attend-political-debates/28188518|title=Gov. LePage says he may not attend political debates|publisher=WMTW |date=September 22, 2014 |access-date=September 22, 2014}} though he was still willing to debate Cutler alone.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/22/politics/lepage-says-he-wont-appear-on-stage-with-michaud/?ref=comments|title=LePage casts doubt on debates, says he won't appear on stage with Michaud|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=September 22, 2014 |access-date=September 22, 2014}} He said he did not want to share a stage with Michaud due to his not having criticized a TV advertisement by a liberal PAC publicizing a press release where LePage called Social Security "welfare, pure and simple," which LePage later stated was not what he meant. LePage said that he used to respect Michaud but called the lack of criticism "sad". Michaud responded by issuing a statement saying that LePage was looking for an excuse to avoid debates and that he should instead use them "to set the record straight and explain why he said in a press release that Social Security is 'welfare' and why Maine's economy hasn't recovered as quickly as the rest of the country." Michaud went on to state that "It's not a gubernatorial debate without the Governor." Cutler issued a statement that both the other men should "stop playing games". Michaud stated the following day at a press conference that he would attend the six debates that his campaign agreed to, regardless of what LePage does. He stated that he expected LePage would attend once his "temper tantrum" was over.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/23/politics/michaud-refuses-to-apologize-for-independent-ad-criticizing-lepage-says-he-will-appear-in-all-debates/|title=Michaud refuses to denounce ad criticizing LePage, calls governor's opposition a 'temper tantrum'|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=September 23, 2014 |access-date=September 23, 2014}} LePage announced on September 28 that he would participate in five debates, saying "This decision has come after much reflection over the past week on the value in debating Congressman Michael Michaud, who has continually been dishonest with the Maine people about Governor LePage's stance on Social Security", and saying he wanted to set the record straight.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/28/politics/lepage-reverses-position-will-participate-in-5-debates/|title=LePage reverses position, will participate in 5 debates|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=September 23, 2014 |access-date=September 28, 2014}} ===Endorsements=== {{Endorsements box | title = Paul LePage | list = '''Politicians''' * [[Rick Bennett (politician)|Rick Bennett]], [[Maine Republican Party]] chairman, former [[List of Presidents of the Maine Senate|president]] of the [[Maine Senate]], 2012 US Senate candidate{{cite web|url=http://lepage2014.com/videos/|title=Re-Elect Governor Paul LePage|access-date=November 15, 2014}} * [[Barbara Bush]], former [[First Lady of the United States]]{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/10/23/politics/elections/george-h-w-bush-endorses-lepage-for-governor/ |title=George H.W. '''Schauer:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584CDE|70–80%}} | title = [[Governor of Michigan|Governor]] | before_election = [[Rick Snyder]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Rick Snyder]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States)| | map = {{switcher |[[file:2014 Michigan gubernatorial election results map by county.svg|300px]] |County results |[[file:2014 Michigan gubernatorial election results map by congressional district.svg|300px]] |Congressional district results }} }} {{ElectionsMI}} The '''2014 Michigan gubernatorial election''' took place on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[governor of Michigan]], concurrently with the [[United States Senate election in Michigan, 2014|election]] of Michigan's [[Classes of United States senators|Class II U.S. Senate seat]], [[2014 United States Senate elections|other elections]] to the United States Senate in other states, [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections|elections]] to the [[United States House of Representatives]], and various [[2014 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2014 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]]. This was one of nine Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[Rick Snyder]] ran for election to a second term in office. Primary elections took place on August 5, 2014, in which Snyder and former U.S. representative [[Mark Schauer]] were unopposed in the Republican and Democratic primaries, respectively.{{cite web|url=http://miboecfr.nictusa.com/election/candlist/14PRI/14PRI_CL.HTM |title=2014 Official Michigan Primary Candidate Listing |publisher=Miboecfr.nictusa.com |date=2014-07-31 |access-date=2014-08-04}} Snyder was considered vulnerable in his bid for a second term, as reflected in his low approval ratings.{{cite news|url=http://www.governing.com/blogs/politics/gov-handicapping-2013-2014-governors-races-tossups.html|title=Handicapping the 2013–2014 Governors Races: The Tossups|newspaper=Governing|date=July 18, 2013|access-date=February 26, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130805052422/http://www.governing.com/blogs/politics/gov-handicapping-2013-2014-governors-races-tossups.html|archive-date=August 5, 2013|df=mdy-all}}{{cite news|url=http://www.dailytribune.com/government-and-politics/20140128/michigan-gov-rick-snyder-raises-5m-in-2013-for-re-election-bid|title=Michigan Gov. Rick Snyder raises $5M in 2013 for re-election bid|newspaper=Daily Tribune|date=January 28, 2014|access-date=February 26, 2014|archive-date=March 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304064720/http://www.dailytribune.com/government-and-politics/20140128/michigan-gov-rick-snyder-raises-5m-in-2013-for-re-election-bid|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|url=http://fivethirtyeight.blogs.nytimes.com/2013/04/08/which-governors-are-most-vulnerable-in-2014/|title=Which Governors Are Most Vulnerable in 2014?|newspaper=Five Thirty Eight|date=April 8, 2013|access-date=February 26, 2014}}{{cite news|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/michigan-governor-poll_n_4235845|title=Michigan Governor Poll Shows Close Race Between Rick Snyder, Mark Schauer|newspaper=[[The Huffington Post]]|last=Woods|first=Ashley|date=November 8, 2013|archive-date=November 9, among ''[[The Cook Political Report]]'',{{cite web|url=http://cookpolitical.com/governor/charts/race-ratings|title=Ratings|access-date=September 6, 2013|archive-date=March 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130305115607/http://cookpolitical.com/governor/charts/race-ratings|url-status=dead}} ''[[Governing (magazine)|Governing]]'',{{cite web |last=Jacobson |first=Louis |url=http://www.governing.com/blogs/politics/gov-handicapping-2013-2014-governors-races-tossups.html |title=Handicapping the 2013–2014 Governors Races: The Tossups |publisher=Governing.com |date=July 18, 2013 |access-date=July 25, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130805052422/http://www.governing.com/blogs/politics/gov-handicapping-2013-2014-governors-races-tossups.html |archive-date=August 5, 2013 |df=mdy-all }} ''[[Stuart Rothenberg|The Rothenberg Political Report]]'',{{cite web|url=http://rothenbergpoliticalreport.com/ratings/governor|title=Ratings|access-date=September 6, 2013}} and ''[[Sabato's Crystal Ball]]''{{cite web|url=http://www.centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/articles/category/2014-governor/|title=Ratings|access-date=September 6, 2013|archive-date=September 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130910081704/http://www.centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/articles/category/2014-governor/|url-status=dead}} was that the contest was a "tossup". Snyder was saddled with a negative approval rating, while his Democratic opponent, former U.S. representative [[Mark Schauer]], suffered from a lack of name recognition.{{cite news|url=http://www.mlive.com/politics/index.ssf/2013/12/poll_michigan_gov_rick_snyder_4.html|title=Poll: Michigan Gov. Rick Snyder, Democrat Mark Schauer in close race ahead of 2014|newspaper=[[MLive Media Group]]|last=Oosting|first=Jonathan|date=December 10, 2013|access-date=December 29, 2013}}{{cite news|url=http://www.freep.com/article/20140828/COL04/308280194/Michigan-Governor-race|title=Brian Dickerson: Can Schauer avoid the Tomb of the Unknown Front-Runner?|newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|first=Brian|last=Dickerson|date=August 28, 2014|access-date=August 28, 2014}} Despite having a more centrist voting record in the House of Representatives,{{cite web|title= Rep. Mark Schauer Former Representative for Michigan's 7th District|url= https://www.govtrack.us/congress/members/mark_schauer/412313}} Schauer ran as more of a populist who put education, unions and taxes as his top priorities.{{cite web|date= October 28, 2014|title= Old-style populism lives on in Michigan race|url= https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/politics/old-style-populism-lives-on-in-michigan-race/}} Despite concerns about his approval rating hurting his chances at victory, Snyder was re-elected with 50.9% of the vote. As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this is the last time a Republican, and a male was elected governor of Michigan, and the last time the Republican candidate won the counties of [[Kalamazoo County, Michigan|Kalamazoo]], [[Oakland County, Michigan|Oakland]], [[Clinton County, Michigan|Clinton]], [[Macomb County, Michigan|Macomb]], [[Kent County, Michigan|Kent]], [[Leelanau County, Michigan|Leelanau]], and [[Isabella County, Michigan|Isabella]], and the last time the Democratic candidate won the counties of [[Alger County, Michigan|Alger]], [[Baraga County, Michigan|Baraga]], and [[Manistee County, Michigan|Manistee]]. This is also the last time that the winner of the Michigan gubernatorial election won a majority of counties, and the first time since 1990 that Michigan simultaneously voted for gubernatorial and U.S. Senate candidates of different political parties. ==Republican primary== Polling indicated significant opposition from Republican primary voters in Michigan towards Snyder's bid for re-election.{{cite web|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/article/20130731/POLITICS02/307300123/1022/politics/Snyder-s-approval-rating-gets-boost-from-bankruptcy-Medicaid-decisions|title=Snyder's approval rating gets boost from bankruptcy, Medicaid decisions|date=July 31, 2013|access-date=August 1, 2013|archive-date=September 27, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927124716/http://www.detroitnews.com/article/20130731/POLITICS02/307300123/1022/politics/Snyder-s-approval-rating-gets-boost-from-bankruptcy-Medicaid-decisions|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.theoaklandpress.com/article/20130903/NEWS/130909949/poll-says-michigan-govrick-snyder-vulnerable-in-a-republican-primary|title=Poll says Michigan Gov. '''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = [[Governor of Minnesota|Governor]] | before_election = [[Mark Dayton]] | before_party = Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party | after_election = [[Mark Dayton]] | after_party = Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party }} {{Elections in Minnesota sidebar}} The '''2014 Minnesota gubernatorial election''' took place on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[governor of Minnesota]]. It was held concurrently with the [[2014 United States Senate election in Minnesota|election]] to Minnesota's [[Classes of United States senators|Class II U.S. Senate seat]], as well as [[2014 United States Senate elections|other elections]] to the United States Senate in other states, [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections|elections]] to the [[United States House of Representatives]], and various [[2014 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2014 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]]. Incumbent [[Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party|Democratic–Farmer–Labor]] governor [[Mark Dayton]] ran for re-election to a second term in office.{{cite web |url=http://www.kare11.com/news/news_article.aspx?storyid=946522 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130127060207/http://www.kare11.com/news/news_article.aspx?storyid=946522 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 27, 2013 |title=Gov. Dayton stops by KARE 11 Sunrise, says he'll run again in 2014 |date=November 15, 2011 |access-date=November 17, 2012 |work=[[KARE (TV)|KARE]]}} Incumbent Democratic lieutenant governor [[Yvonne Prettner Solon]] retired, and Tina Smith was selected as his new running mate.{{cite news |author=Brian Bakst |title=Minn. Lt. Gov. Prettner Solon says no to 2nd term |newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |url=http://www.sfgate.com/news/article/Minn-LG-Prettner-Solon-says-no-to-2nd-term-5141482.php |date=January 14, 2014 |access-date=January 14, 2014}} Primary elections were held on August 12, 2014. Dayton and Smith won the Democratic primary and the Republicans nominated [[Hennepin County, Minnesota|Hennepin County]] [[County commission|Commissioner]] [[Jeff Johnson (Minnesota politician)|Jeff Johnson]] and his running mate former state representative [[Bill Kuisle]]. In the general election, Dayton and Smith defeated them and several other minor party candidates with just over 50% of the vote. Dayton's victory broke his own record, set in 2010, as the oldest Minnesota gubernatorial candidate to win an election; he was 67.{{cite web |url=http://editions.lib.umn.edu/smartpolitics/2014/11/13/minnesotans-elect-oldest-gover/ |title=Minnesotans Elect Oldest Governor, US House Delegation in State History |work=Smart Politics |first=Eric |last=Ostermeier |date=November 13, 2014}} It was also the first gubernatorial race since [[1994 Minnesota gubernatorial election|1994]] in which the winner received a majority of the votes cast. The election was the first time since 1994 that a [[Third party (United States)|third party]] did not gain more than 6% of the total vote. ==Background== Incumbent [[Republican Party of Minnesota|Republican]] governor [[Tim Pawlenty]] declined to run for a third term [[2010 Minnesota gubernatorial election|in 2010]], instead [[Tim Pawlenty 2012 presidential campaign|running for the Republican presidential nomination]] in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 election]]. State Representative [[Tom Emmer]] easily won the Republican nomination, and former U.S. senator [[Mark Dayton]] won the DFL nomination with a plurality over [[List of Speakers of the Minnesota House of Representatives|State House Speaker]] [[Margaret Anderson Kelliher]]. After a very close race, Dayton defeated Emmer by just 8,770 votes, 0.42% of all votes cast. Dayton's victory was one of just four that Minnesota Democrats have achieved out of 28 gubernatorial elections during a Democratic presidency.{{cite web |url=http://editions.lib.umn.edu/smartpolitics/2013/12/06/can-dayton-catch-lightning-in/ |title=Can Dayton Catch Lightning in a Bottle Twice? |work=Smart Politics |first=Eric |last=Ostermeier |date=December 6, 2013}} Despite this, and despite his narrow margin of victory in 2010, Dayton was not seen as a top Republican target. '''Hassebrook:''' {{legend0|#A5B0FF|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996E2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674DE|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584CDE|70–80%}} {{legend0|#3933E5|80–90%}} {{legend0|#0D0596|90%+}}
'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#D2B1D9|40–50%}} | title = [[Governor of Nebraska|Governor]] | before_election = [[Dave Heineman]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Pete Ricketts]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsNE}} The '''2014 Nebraska gubernatorial election''' took place on Tuesday, November 4, 2014, to elect the 40th [[Governor of Nebraska]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Candidate and former COO of [[TD Ameritrade]] [[Pete Ricketts]] defeated [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate and former [[University of Nebraska system|Regent of the University of Nebraska]] Chuck Hassebrook, receiving 57.2% of the vote to Hassebrook's 39.2%{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/2014-election/results/map/governor/nebraska/|title=Nebraska Governor's race results|work=[[Politico]]|date=November 7, 2014|access-date=November 10, 2014}} This was the first open seat election, and the first time a Democrat won a county for governor since [[1998 Nebraska gubernatorial election|1998]]. ==Republican primary== [[Lieutenant Governor of Nebraska|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Rick Sheehy]] first declared his intention to run for governor in July 2011.{{cite web|url=http://journalstar.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/sheehy-says-he-will-run-for-nebraska-governor-in/article_ac9f1f70-132f-5e8b-ab5f-1b07ade93c23.html|title=Sheehy says he will run for Nebraska governor in 2014|date=July 15, 2011|access-date=August 12, 2013|work=Journal Star}} Considered to be the "hand-picked" successor to incumbent Governor [[Dave Heineman]], he was endorsed by him.{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/article/20120807/NEWS/708089977/1688|title=Mike Flood still considering run for Nebraska governor|date=August 8, 2012|access-date=August 12, 2013|work=Omaha.com|archive-date=August 11, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120811010805/http://www.omaha.com/article/20120807/NEWS/708089977/1688|url-status=dead}} Sheehy was joined in the Republican primary by Speaker of the [[Nebraska Legislature]] [[Mike Flood (Nebraska politician)|Mike Flood]] in November 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/article/20121112/NEWS/711139950/1685|title=Mike Flood launches bid for governor's office in 2014|date=November 12, 2012|access-date=August 12, 2013|work=Omaha.com|archive-date=December 4, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204235112/http://www.omaha.com/article/20121112/NEWS/711139950/1685|url-status=dead}} Flood withdrew from the race less than a month later after his wife was diagnosed with breast cancer.{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/article/20121206/NEWS/121209787|title=Mike Flood drops bid for governor; wife ill|date=December 6, 2012|access-date=August 12, 2013|work=Omaha.com|archive-date=November 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110072931/http://www.omaha.com/article/20121206/NEWS/121209787|url-status=dead}} Sheehy resigned as Lieutenant Governor and withdrew from the race in February 2013 after the ''[[Omaha World-Herald]]'' discovered that he had made 2,300 phone calls on a state-issued phone, many of them long and at night, to four women, none of whom were his wife.{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/article/20130203/NEWS/702039876#sheehy-steps-aside-after-phone-records-reveal-2-300-calls-to-4-women|title=Sheehy steps aside after phone records reveal 2,300 calls to 4 women|date=February 4, 2013|access-date=August 12, 2013|work=Omaha.com|archive-date=November 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110072925/http://www.omaha.com/article/20130203/NEWS/702039876#sheehy-steps-aside-after-phone-records-reveal-2-300-calls-to-4-women|url-status=dead}} At the end of the month, Flood was reported to be reconsidering his decision with his wife progressing well in her treatment. In July he announced that he would not re-enter the race. Cattle rancher [[Charles W. Herbster]], who had not formally entered the race but had been campaigning since July, became the third Republican to withdraw when he withdrew on August 23. He cited the health of his wife, who had recently undergone heart surgery.{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/article/20130823/NEWS/130829502/1688#surprises-in-governor-s-race-herbster-out-mccoy-in|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130827141915/http://www.omaha.com/article/20130823/NEWS/130829502/1688%23surprises-in-governor-s-race-herbster-out-mccoy-in|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 27, 2013|title=Surprises in governor's race: Herbster out; McCoy in|date=August 24, 2013|access-date=August 27, 2013|work=Omaha.com|author=Robynn Tysver}} In September 2013, Omaha businessman [[Pete Ricketts]] joined the race. Ricketts, a former chief operating officer of [[TD Ameritrade]] and the son of company founder [[Joe Ricketts]], had run unsuccessfully in 2006 for the U.S. Senate seat held by [[Ben Nelson]].Walton, Don. [http://journalstar.com/news/state-and-regional/statehouse/ricketts-looks-forward-to-changing-skeptics-minds/article_9baf6806-3bce-55d4-92ea-31671b3870d8.html "Ricketts looks forward to changing skeptics' minds".] [http://journalstar.com/ ''Lincoln Journal Star''.] September 8, 2013. Retrieved 2015-02-10. State Senator [[Charlie Janssen]], who had lagged in endorsements and fundraising, withdrew from the race on February 3, 2014. He said: "The way the field was shaping up, I didn't see a clear path to victory."{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/article/20140203/NEWS/140209627/1685#charlie-janssen-abandons-his-bid-for-governor|title=Charlie Janssen abandons his bid for governor|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=February 3, 2014|work=[[Omaha World-Herald]]|first=Robynn|last=Tysver|archive-date=February 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140220205500/http://www.omaha.com/article/20140203/NEWS/140209627/1685#charlie-janssen-abandons-his-bid-for-governor|url-status=dead}} He later declared his candidacy for State Auditor. In February 2014, state attorney general [[Jon Bruning]] announced that he was joining the race. His entry made him the perceived front-runner, supplanting Ricketts, who had been regarded as the leading contender up to that time.Tsyver, Robynn. [http://www.omaha.com/news/attorney-general-jon-bruning-to-run-for-nebraska-governor/article_ab723baf-1afe-5b8b-92fe-3da3ea24aff2.html#attorney-general-jon-bruning-to-run-for-nebraska-governor "Attorney General Jon Bruning to run for Nebraska governor".] [http://www.omaha.com/ ''Omaha World-Herald''.] February 9, 2014. Retrieved 2015-02-10. In the May 13 Republican primary, Ricketts narrowly defeated Bruning, with 26.5% of the vote to Bruning's 25.5%. Elworth, Jr. | party = Libertarian Party (United States) | votes = 402 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 402 | percentage= 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==General election== ===Debates=== ====September 1 debate==== Chuck Hassebrook and Pete Ricketts sparred over education policy, economics and full-time residency in Lincoln at the Nebraska State Fair. Hassebrook opposed school vouchers for public school students, suggesting that tax dollars should be used to improve public schools. Ricketts countered that a gradual voucher policy would help students while keeping money in public schools. The duo showed stark differences in economic policy, with Hassebrook supporting a minimum wage increase and Ricketts opposing an increased wage. Moderator Mike'l Severe asked both candidates if they would reside in the [[Nebraska Governor's Mansion|governor's mansion]] full-time if elected. Ricketts, who has three children attending school in Omaha, said that he had not made a final decision on the question. Hassebrook stated that Nebraska needs a "full-time governor" and that he would live in Lincoln because "40 hours a week is a vacation."{{Cite web|url=https://omaha.com/news/local/hassebrook-ricketts-debate-nebraskas-governor-candidates-display-stark-choice-voters-will-face/article_be2fa1fc-3233-11e4-95b5-0017a43b2370.html|title=Hassebrook-Ricketts debate: Nebraska's governor candidates display stark choice voters will face|first=Robynn Tysver / World-Herald staff|last=writer|website=Omaha World-Herald|date=September 2, 2014 }} ====October 2 debate==== The two candidates traded barbs over past positions in a debate sponsored by Nebraska Educational Communications. Hassebrook accused Ricketts of supporting [[Dave Heineman|Gov. Dave Heineman's]] (R) tax proposal in 2013, which would have increased sales tax rates. The Platte Institute, a conservative think-tank created by Ricketts, supported the tax proposal, which ultimately failed to pass in the face of increasing public criticism. Hassebrook argued that Ricketts tried to hide his support for the measure when he decided to run for governor. Ricketts denied support for the bill, noting that he did not agree with every position taken by the institute.{{Cite web|url=https://omaha.com/news/state_and_regional/in-their-last-debate-before-election-nebraska-governor-candidates-try-to-build-contrasts/article_35e3e5de-4a9c-11e4-b7a3-0017a43b2370.html|title=In their last debate before election, Nebraska governor candidates try to build contrasts|first=Robynn|last=Tysver|website=Omaha World-Herald|date=October 2, 2014 }} Ricketts countered by bringing up a report co-authored by Hassebrook in 1990 that called for a ban on exports of [[genetically modified crops]]. The issue of biotechnology in farming has grown in prominence due to the importance of Nebraska's agricultural sector. Hassebrook responded that he provided little assistance to the authors of the report, and was wrongly credited as a co-author. He also noted that he supported biotechnology research since the early 1990s, when he served on the University of Nebraska Board of Regents. Debate viewers also saw Hassebrook and Ricketts stake out distinct positions on immigration and the proposed [[Keystone Pipeline|Keystone XL]] pipeline that would run through Nebraska. Hassebrook advocated for allowing driving licenses for children brought to the country illegally, while Ricketts opposed issuing licenses as a matter of protecting existing laws. Ricketts suggested that the XL Pipeline would bring jobs to the state and securely transport oil across the country, citing problems with rail transportation of oil. Hassebrook opposed the pipeline because he suggested the project would contribute to climate change. *[https://www.c-span.org/video/?321740-1/nebraska-governors-debate Complete video of debate] ===Candidates=== In Nebraska, gubernatorial nominees select their running mates after the primary elections. * [[Pete Ricketts]] (Republican), former [[Chief Operating Officer|COO]] of [[TD Ameritrade]] and nominee for the U.S. Senate in [[United States Senate election in Nebraska, 2006|2006]] :* Running mate: [[Mike Foley (Nebraska politician)|Mike Foley]], Nebraska Auditor of Public Accounts. Ricketts had initially selected incumbent Lieutenant Governor [[Lavon Heidemann]] as his running mate, but Heidemann resigned from office and withdrew from the election on September 9, 2014, after allegations of domestic abuse. Ricketts named Foley as his new running mate within hours and, after some initial confusion as to whether Heidemann's name would still appear on the ballot,{{cite web|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/09/09/lavon-heidemann-resigns_n_5791054.html|title=Nebraska Lt. Governor Lavon Heidemann Resigns Following Domestic Abuse Allegations|date=September 9, 2014|access-date=September 9, 2014|agency=[[Associated Press]]|first=Grant|last=Schulte|website=[[HuffPost]] }}{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/news/metro/pete-ricketts-chooses-mike-foley-as-running-mate/article_11a24050-383e-11e4-ac0d-0017a43b2370.html|title=Pete Ricketts moves quickly to pick Mike Foley as running mate, but is it fast enough to get name on ballot?|date=September 9, 2014|access-date=September 10, 2014|work=Omaha.com|author=Robynn Tysver}} [[Secretary of State of Nebraska|Secretary of State]] [[John A. '''Havenstein:''' {{legend0|#FFB2B2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#E27F7F|50–60%}} {{legend0|#D75D5D|60–70%}} {{legend0|#D72F30|70–80%}} {{legend0|#a80000|>90%}} | title = [[Governor of New Hampshire|Governor]] | before_election = [[Maggie Hassan]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Maggie Hassan]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsNH}} The '''2014 New Hampshire gubernatorial election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[governor of New Hampshire]], concurrently with the [[United States Senate election in New Hampshire, 2014|election]] to New Hampshire's [[Classes of United States senators|Class II U.S. Senate seat]], as well as other elections to the [[2014 United States Senate elections|United States Senate]] in other states and elections to the [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections|United States House of Representatives]] and various state and local elections. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Maggie Hassan]] ran for re-election to a second term in office. She defeated the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee, businessman [[Walt Havenstein]]. As of {{Year}}, this is the last time a Democrat was elected Governor of New Hampshire. Hassan would retire in 2016 to run successfully for the [[2016 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|Senate]]. ==Background== Incumbent Democratic governor [[John Lynch (New Hampshire governor)|John Lynch]] decided to retire [[2012 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|in 2012]], rather than seek re-election to a fifth term in office. The Democratic nominee, former [[New Hampshire Senate|State Senate]] Majority Leader [[Maggie Hassan]], defeated the Republican nominee, attorney and [[1996 United States gubernatorial elections|1996]] gubernatorial nominee [[Ovide M. Lamontagne]], 55% to 43%. New Hampshire and [[Vermont]] are the only states in the country whose governors are elected every two years. On only one occasion since 1924 has a first-term governor of New Hampshire been defeated for re-election to a second term: in [[2004 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|2004]], when Lynch beat incumbent Republican governor [[Craig Benson]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wmur.com/news/politics/poll-job-approval-ratings-rise-for-hassan/-/9857748/21267234/-/154vlhj/-/index.html|title=Poll: Job approval ratings rise for Hassan|date=July 31, 2013|access-date=August 2, 2013|work=WMUR}}Schweitzer, Sarah (November 4, 2004). "[http://archive.boston.com/news/politics/governors/articles/2004/11/04/defeated_after_1_term_nh_governor_fades_out/ Defeated after 1 term, N.H. governor fades out]". ''[[The Boston Globe]]''. Retrieved on February 6, 2011. Hassan had high approval ratings. An April 2014 [[WMUR-TV|WMUR]]/[[University of New Hampshire]] poll found that 57% of registered voters approved of the job she was doing, 58% had a favorable opinion of her, and 70% thought the state was going in the right direction.{{cite web|url=http://cola.unh.edu/sites/cola.unh.edu/files/research_publications/gsp2013_fall_govapp102413.pdf|title=APPROVAL OF HASSAN AND LEGISLATURE REMAINS HIGH, MOST THINK NH IS ON RIGHT TRACK|date=October 24, 2013|access-date=February 3, 2014|work=WMUR/UNH|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221013332/http://cola.unh.edu/sites/cola.unh.edu/files/research_publications/gsp2013_fall_govapp102413.pdf|archive-date=February 21, 2014|url-status=dead}} For these reasons, Hassan was not considered vulnerable going into the election. '''Tie:''' {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50%}} | title = [[List of governors of New Mexico|Governor]] | before_election = [[Susana Martínez]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Susana Martínez]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | map = {{switcher|[[File:2014 New Mexico gubernatorial election results map by county.svg|230px]]| County results|[[File:2014 New Mexico gubernatorial election results map by congressional district.svg|230px]]|Congressional district results |[[File:2014 New Mexico gubernatorial election by precinct.svg|230px]] |Precinct results}} }} {{Elections in New Mexico sidebar}} The '''2014 New Mexico gubernatorial election''' took place on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[List of governors of New Mexico|governor of New Mexico]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[Susana Martínez]] successfully ran for election to a second term in office, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[Attorney General of New Mexico|Attorney General]] [[Gary King (politician)|Gary King]]. This was one of nine Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]]. Unlike in most states, New Mexico's governor and lieutenant governor are elected in [[2014 New Mexico elections#Lieutenant Governor|separate primaries]]. The winning candidates then run together on the same ticket. Primary elections were held on June 3, 2014. As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this is the last time that Republicans won a non-judicial statewide election in New Mexico, and stands as the best performance by a Republican gubernatorial candidate in New Mexico history.{{Cite web |title=Our Campaigns - Container Detail Page |url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/ContainerHistory.html?ContainerID=187 |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=www.ourcampaigns.com}} This is also the last time that the winner of the New Mexico gubernatorial election won a majority of counties. ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * [[Susana Martínez]], incumbent governor{{cite web|url=http://www.abqjournal.com/282286/news/gov-susana-martinez-raises-2m-for-re-election.htm|title=Gov. '''Astorino:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}} | title = [[Governor of New York|Governor]] | before_election = [[Andrew Cuomo]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Andrew Cuomo]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }}{{ElectionsNY}} The '''2014 New York gubernatorial election''' took place on November 4, 2014. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Andrew Cuomo]] sought re-election to a second term in office, though incumbent lieutenant governor [[Robert Duffy (politician)|Robert Duffy]] did not seek re-election. Cuomo and his running mate, former U.S. representative [[Kathy Hochul]], won contested primaries, while [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Rob Astorino]], the [[Westchester County Executive]], and his running mate ([[Chemung County, New York|Chemung County]] Sheriff Chris Moss) were unopposed for their party's nomination. Astorino and Moss were also cross-nominated by the [[Conservative Party of New York State|Conservative Party]] and the Stop Common Core Party. Democrat [[Andrew Cuomo]], then serving as [[Attorney General of New York]], was elected governor [[2010 New York gubernatorial election|in 2010]]. Cuomo defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] businessman [[Carl Paladino]] by a nearly 2-to-1 margin, 63% to 33%. Cuomo succeeded retiring Democratic governor [[David Paterson]]. Entering the 2014 campaign, Cuomo enjoyed high approval ratings and a large campaign war chest that totaled $33 million as of January 2014. [[The Cook Political Report]], Daily Kos Elections, [[Governing (magazine)|Governing]], [[RealClearPolitics]], [[Stuart Rothenberg|The Rothenberg Political Report]], and [[Sabato's Crystal Ball]] all rated the 2014 New York gubernatorial election as "Safe Democratic". On Election Day, Cuomo and Hochul defeated Astorino and Moss by a margin of 14 percentage points.{{cite web|url=http://www.elections.ny.gov/NYSBOE/elections/2014/general/2014Governor.pdf|title=NYS Board of Elections Governor/Lt. Governor Election Returns November 4, 2014|access-date=September 5, 2018|archive-date=November 7, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181107185927/http://www.elections.ny.gov/NYSBOE/elections/2014/general/2014Governor.pdf|url-status=dead}} This is the last gubernatorial election in which the counties of [[Clinton County, New York|Clinton]], [[Franklin County, New York|Franklin]], and [[Essex County, New York|Essex]] voted Democratic, and the last in which [[Monroe County, New York|Monroe]] and [[Ulster County, New York|Ulster]] voted Republican. ==Democratic primary== Progressive minor parties saw an opportunity to make headway in the state due to Cuomo's relatively conservative stances on taxes and spending.{{cite news| url=https://www.governing.com/news/headlines/gov-andrew-cuomo-isnt-getting-a-coronation-in-new-york.html|title=Andrew Cuomo Is Going to Win but Not with the Landslide He Wants | work=Governing | author=Alan Greenblatt | date=September 5, 2014 | access-date=September 20, 2014}}{{cite news|url=https://www.nationaljournal.com/politics/gov-cuomo-suffers-discomfort-even-as-n-y-democrats-power-swells-20140908|title=Gov. [http://www.timesunion.com/local/article/Third-party-s-profile-rises-5921969.php Third party's profile rises]. ''Times Union''. Retrieved November 29, 2014. Cuomo carried New York City 77.08% to 17.47% (782,911 votes to 177,450 votes), while narrowly losing the Upstate 45.89% to 48.49% (1,286,569 votes to 1,359,429 votes). The Green Party took Row D on the ballot, surpassing the Independence and Working Families Parties (both of whom lost significant vote share but still [[qualified New York parties|qualified for automatic ballot status]] through 2018) but not surpassing the Conservative Party, which retained Row C with 6 percent of the vote. The Libertarian Party, after a 2010 showing in which it narrowly fell short of the 50,000 votes needed for automatic ballot access, missed that measure by a wide margin in 2014; the Party's candidate earned less than 17,000 votes. The Sapient Party was a non-factor with fewer than 5,000 votes. Two new political parties—the Women's Equality Party and the Stop Common Core Party—surpassed the 50,000-vote threshold and attained automatic ballot status.{{cite news|url=https://www.newsday.com/long-island/politics/spin-cycle/leading-gop-ers-eye-setup-for-new-stop-common-core-party-1.9612314|title=Leading GOP'ers eye setup for new 'Stop Common Core' party|work=Newsday|last=Janison|first=Dan|date=November 12, 2014|access-date=September 5, 2018|archive-date=September 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906052604/https://www.newsday.com/long-island/politics/spin-cycle/leading-gop-ers-eye-setup-for-new-stop-common-core-party-1.9612314|url-status=dead}} ==References== {{Reflist|3}} ==External links== *[https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_gubernatorial_election,_2014 New York gubernatorial election, 2014] at [[Ballotpedia]] *[http://www.followthemoney.org/database/StateGlance/state_candidates.phtml?s=NY&y=2014&f=G Campaign contributions] at FollowTheMoney.org {{2014 United States elections}} {{New York elections}} [[Category:2014 elections in New York (state)|Gubernatorial]] [[Category:New York (state) gubernatorial elections|2014]] [[Category:2014 United States gubernatorial elections|New York]] [[Category:Andrew Cuomo]] [[Category:Howie Hawkins]] [[Category:November 2014 in the United States]]

'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No data}} | title = [[Governor of Ohio|Governor]] | before_election = [[John Kasich]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[John Kasich]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 40.65% (registered voters) {{decrease}}8.57pp }} {{ElectionsOH}} The '''2014 Ohio gubernatorial election''' took place on November 4, 2014. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[John Kasich]] won a second term by a landslide over [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate [[Ed FitzGerald]] and [[Green Party (United States)|Green Party]] candidate [[Anita Rios]]. [[Partisan primary|Primary elections]] were held on May 6, 2014. Kasich's [[landslide victory]] gave him the highest percentage of the vote since [[George Voinovich]]'s win in [[1994 Ohio gubernatorial election|1994]], a large improvement from his narrow victory in [[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|2010]]. {{As of|2024}}, this was the last time the counties of [[Cuyahoga County, Ohio|Cuyahoga]] and [[Franklin County, Ohio|Franklin]] voted for the Republican candidate and the last time [[Monroe County, Ohio|Monroe County]] voted for the Democratic candidate. This was one of the nine Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]]. ==Background== Kasich, who was elected with [[Tea Party movement|Tea Party]] support [[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|in 2010]], faced considerable backlash from the movement. His decision to accept the [[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act]]'s expansion of [[Medicaid]], his increased spending, taxation of [[Hydraulic fracturing|fracking]] on Ohio farmland and perceived failure to go far enough on charter schools and school vouchers caused Tea Party groups to refuse to support his campaign.{{cite web|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/john-kasich-tea-party_n_2854815|title=John Kasich Faces Tea Party Protest Over Medicaid Decision|date=March 11, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013|work=HuffPost|first=Amanda|archive-date=March 14, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314034346/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/03/11/john-kasich-tea-party_n_2854815.html|url-status=live|last=Terkel}} When Kasich passed over Tea Party leader Tom Zawistowski for the position of executive director of the [[Ohio Republican Party]] in favor of [[Matt Borges]], who worked with a gay rights group, that was widely seen as the last straw.{{cite news|url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2013/05/06/why-does-the-tea-party-want-to-let-democrats-run-ohio.html|title=Why Does the Tea Party Want to Let Democrats Run Ohio?|date=May 6, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013|work=The Daily Beast|first=Justin|last=Green}} Tea Party groups announced they would support a primary challenger, or, if none emerged, the [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] nominee. Zawistowski said, "John Kasich is going to lose in 2014. We don't care who else wins."{{cite news|url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2013/09/04/ohio-republican-party-goes-to-war-with-itself-leaving-2016-in-doubt.html|title=Ohio Republican Party Goes to War With Itself, Leaving 2016 in Doubt|date=September 4, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013|work=The Daily Beast|first=David|last=Freedlander}} Ultimately, Kasich was unopposed in the Republican '''Dorman:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = [[Governor of Oklahoma|Governor]] | before_election = [[Mary Fallin]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Mary Fallin]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsOK}} The '''2014 Oklahoma gubernatorial election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[governor of Oklahoma]]. Incumbent Governor [[Mary Fallin]] was re-elected with 55.8% of the vote over state Representative [[Joe Dorman]]. Primaries were held on June 24, 2014. Fallin won the Republican nomination with more than 75% of the vote, and Dorman won the Democratic nomination uncontested. ==Republican primary== Fallin, the incumbent, easily defeated Chad "The Drug Lawyer" Moody, and Dax Ewbank, who would run as a [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] for [[2016 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|U.S. Senate in 2016]]. Ewbank and Moody both stressed ending the [[war on drugs]] and protecting [[Right to bear arms|2nd Amendment rights]].{{Cite web|url=http://newsok.com/article/4949222|title=Fallin faces two candidates '''Kitzhaber:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}}
'''Richardson:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}} | title = [[Governor of Oregon|Governor]] | before_election = [[John Kitzhaber]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[John Kitzhaber]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsOR}} The '''2014 Oregon gubernatorial election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[Governor of Oregon]], concurrently with other [[2014 Oregon state elections|elections in Oregon]] and [[2014 United States elections|across the United States]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party of Oregon|Democrat]] [[John Kitzhaber]] defeated [[Oregon Republican Party|Republican]] state legislator [[Dennis Richardson (politician)|Dennis Richardson]], winning his fourth overall, and second consecutive, four-year term as governor.{{cite news |title=John Kitzhaber asks Oregon lawmakers to leave behind 'difficult campaign,' start healing |first=Laura |last=Gunderson |work=The Oregonian |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/politics/index.ssf/2014/11/john_kitzhaber_asksoregon_lawm.html#incart_maj-story-1 |date=November 5, 2014 }} The race was closer than expected due to recent revelations of potential ethical violations involving his fiancée, Cylvia Hayes. Most news outlets called the election in his favor by 9:00 p.m. on election night. Kitzhaber thanked his supporters for a successful race, while Richardson refused to concede due to the close tally.{{cite news |title=Dennis Richardson refuses to concede, John Kitzhaber thanks voters for a fourth term: Oregon election results 2014 |first=Laura |last=Gunderson |date=November 4, 2014 |work=The Oregonian |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/politics/index.ssf/2014/11/dennis_richardson_refuses_to_c.html#incart_story_package }} Four [[third party (United States)|third party]] candidates also appeared on the ballot, with each winning less than 2% of the vote. Kitzhaber and Richardson were nominated in the primary election on May 20, 2014. As of 2022, this is the last gubernatorial election in Oregon where [[Clatsop County, Oregon|Clatsop County]] supported the Republican candidate, the last one where [[Tillamook County, Oregon|Tillamook County]] supported the Democratic candidate, and the last time that a man was elected Governor of Oregon. If Kitzhaber had served his full term, he would have become the second longest-serving governor in U.S. history.{{cite web |url=http://editions.lib.umn.edu/smartpolitics/2013/12/10/kitzhaber-launches-bid-to-beco/ |title= Kitzhaber Launches Bid to Become 2nd Longest-Serving Governor in History |work=Smart Politics |first=Eric |last=Ostermeier |date= December 10, 2013}} However, he resigned on February 18, 2015.{{cite news |last= Nakamura |first= Beth |date= February 13, 2015 |title= Oregon Governor John Kitzhaber resigns amid criminal investigation, growing scandal |url= http://www.oregonlive.com/politics/index.ssf/2015/02/gov_john_kitzhaber_resigns_ami.html#incart_maj-story-1 |newspaper= The Oregonian |location= Portland, Oregon |access-date= February 13, 2015}} ==Background== {{see also|John Kitzhaber|Dennis Richardson (politician)}} Physician and then-[[List of Presidents of the Oregon State Senate|President]] of the [[Oregon State Senate]] [[John Kitzhaber]] was first elected governor in [[1994 Oregon gubernatorial election|1994]] and was re-elected in [[1998 Oregon gubernatorial election|1998]]. [[Term limits in Oregon|Term limits]] prevented him from running in [[2002 Oregon gubernatorial election|2002]]. He considered running in [[2006 Oregon gubernatorial election|2006]] but decided not to; incumbent Democrat [[Ted Kulongoski]] was re-elected. In September 2009, Kitzhaber announced that he would seek a third term as governor [[2010 Oregon gubernatorial election|in 2010]].{{cite news|url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/mapesonpolitics/2009/09/kitzhaber_files_committee_to_r.html|title=Kitzhaber files committee to run for governor|last=Mapes|first=Jeff|date=September 2, 2009|publisher=OregonLive.com}} In May 2010, he won the Democratic primary with 65% of the vote, defeating former secretary of state of Oregon [[Bill Bradbury]].[http://www.kptv.com/yourvote/23601768/detail.html Kitzhaber, Dudley To Face Off For Governor - Your Vote News Story - KPTV Portland] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100704190457/http://www.kptv.com/yourvote/23601768/detail.html |date=2010-07-04 }} After a close general election campaign, Kitzhaber won the election with 49% to Republican nominee [[Chris Dudley]]'s 48%. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * Ifeanyichukwu Chijioke Diru{{cite news|author=Christian Gaston |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/politics/index.ssf/2014/03/election_2014_who_filed_for_st.html | work=[[The Oregonian]] | title=Election 2014: Who filed for Oregon statewide and congressional office | date=March 11, 2014|access-date=March 13, 2014}} * [[John Kitzhaber]], incumbent [[Governor of Oregon|governor]]{{cite news| last=Esteve|first=Harry|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/politics/index.ssf/2013/12/john_kitzhaber_announces_for_h.html | work=[[The Oregonian]] | title=John Kitzhaber announces for historic fourth term | date=December 9, 2013|access-date=December 9, 2013}} ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results{{cite web|url=http://records.sos.state.or.us/ORSOSWebDrawer/RecordView/6873756|title=May 20, 2014 Primary Election Abstract of Votes: Governor|access-date=July 7, 2014|publisher=Oregon Secretary of State|archive-date=October 18, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018004122/http://records.sos.state.or.us/ORSOSWebDrawer/RecordView/6873756|url-status=dead}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = John Kitzhaber (incumbent) | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 268,654 | percentage = 89.0 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Ifeanyichukwu C. Smith]] was re-elected [[United States Senate election in Oregon, 2002|in 2002]] and a Republican has not been elected governor since [[Victor G. Atiyeh]] was re-elected [[1982 Oregon gubernatorial election|in 1982]]. At the annual [[Seaside, Oregon#Annual cultural events|Dorchester Conference]] for activists in March 2013, Oregon Republicans acknowledged the difficulties they faced. At the Conference, "the lack of activity was so pronounced that the conference's Saturday night satirical show ran a video that began with an announcer intoning, "Now we go live to the 2014 Republican governor's debate." The camera then panned over a debate stage with two empty chairs, the monotony broken only by a broom-wielding janitor." High-profile Republicans have all passed on the election and while attendees split on whether the party needed to change its policies, they agreed that the party needed to be a "big tent" again.{{cite web|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/mapes/index.ssf/2013/03/post.html|title=Republicans search for ways to revive GOP brand in Oregon|date=March 10, 2013|access-date=July 25, 2013|work=[[The
